newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Finnair says ex-Sweden air cargo 400 tonnes/week.
newsitem.headline: Finnair says ex-Sweden air cargo 400 tonnes/week.

text.p: Finnish flag-carrier Finnair said on Monday it was trucking about 300 tonnes of air cargo per month to Helsinki from Stockholm in addition to the 100 tonnes of cargo it flew out of Stockholm.
The airline currently flies 42 flights daily from Finland via Stockholm's international airport Arlanda to other European cities.
"On our outgoing export on passenger flights we have roughly 100 tonnes per month," Finnair cargo Swedish district sales manager Karl-Johan Berg told Reuters in an interview.
Berg said the airline may consider stepping up the frequency of its freighter operation between New York, Helsinki and Singapore to two frequencies per week.
"But it still is in its early stages," Berg told Reuters.
Since August 4 last year Finnair has been buying a 90-tonne allotment on an eastward-flying Boeing 747-100F operated by Polar Air Cargo of the United States.
The once-weekly operation has been running as planned since then, an airline spokesman said.
Air cargo rates from Helsinki were higher than from Stockholm, Berg said.

"Finland is actually the better deal for the company. In Finland the rates are higher compared to other marketplaces in Europe," Berg said. He added that in Sweden Finnair air cargo rates tended to be about average compared to other airlines'.

Only about five percent of the cargo traffic volumes the airline flew were flown at special, or ad hoc, rates, while the big Swedish exporters generally made contracts for the duration of a timetable period, Berg said.
Finnair carried 60,000 tonnes of air cargo in its 1995/96 financial year, a rise of around five percent on the previous year's figures while tonne kilometres were up eight percent.
Exports account for roughly half of the airline's cargo.
The Far East accounted for roughly 44 percent of Finnair's cargo earnings, North America accounted for 23 percent, Europe 28 percent and domestic, five percent, the airline said.
